must_fix.what: A known program fault is hidden by narrowing a kept step, and nothing in the code or the docs says so. Retired check_frame_ui asserted '14 -> 16 -> 18 -> 20 -> 28 -> 14 pt: both panes ... come back ... with no ratchet'. The folded step 14 in tools/check_finder_ui.py stops at 20 pt so that it passes. The fault is real and needs only one trip: on a fresh window at 1920x1200, raising the interface size to 28 pt and setting it back to 14 leaves both panes at 415 px in the default look (326 when fresh) and 479 px in the Kasandra look (354 when fresh). The base tree (42a7080) does the same, so the fault came before this patch. The builder's report says 'a direct 14, 28, 14 comes back to 326'; I could not reproduce that, so the fault is wider than reported. SPEC 'rules for keeping or retiring a test' says to retire only when the test catches no bug that no other test catches, and to keep no list of known failures. Here the only step that catches this bug was retired, and its replacement was made to miss it. Fix pane_qt/desk_qt so the panes come back, and take step 14 through 28 pt again, as the retired check did. If the coordinator defers the fix, step 14 and docs/WINDOW_CHECKS.md must at least say plainly why the step stops at 20 pt, and the report and release note must drop the 'direct trip comes back' claim.
must_fix.where: tools/check_finder_ui.py step 14 (for points in (16,18,20)); workbench/pane_qt.py / desk_qt.py (the panes' least width after a size change); builder report not_done and numbers
must_fix.how_to_reproduce: In a copy with the patch and a current seed, run checks/review/bin/ratchet.py <copy> as the gate runs a check (offscreen, unshare, fresh HOME), once with GRAPHITE_NOOP=1 and once with GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE=kasandra. It sets reading.ui_pt to 28 and then 14 through ledger.settings.set + sync_profile + type_bar.align. Output: default 'fresh 14 [326, 326]', 'after (28, 14) [415, 415]'; kasandra 'fresh 14 [354, 354]', 'after (28, 14) [479, 479]'. With git checkout HEAD~1 -- workbench (the base program): the same 326 -> 415.

must_fix.what: Nothing in the unit tests pins the Date Modified fix where it is wired. test_whole_words.ColumnTitles tests only the new helpers finder_qt.column_width and title_need. Its 'fails before' was an AttributeError: the helpers did not exist. I reverted FinderPage.scale_columns to the old width (self.list_widths[column] = round(width * scale)) and kept the helpers. All 5 tests in test_whole_words still pass, in both looks. The only thing that catches the revert is tools/check_finder_ui.py run in the Kasandra look. The gate runs only with --ui, and only in the look in force, which is the default unless GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE is set. So a regression of the program fix would pass the release check's default runs. The binding rule is 'every behaviour you add or fix gets a test that fails before and passes after'. Add a test that builds a FinderPage, or calls scale_columns on one, with a header face wide enough to need more than 120 px, and asserts list.columnWidth(1) >= title_need(header, 1). The test must fail when scale_columns ignores the need.
must_fix.how_to_reproduce: In the patched copy: replace 'self.list_widths[column] = column_width(width, scale, need)' with 'self.list_widths[column] = round(width * scale)' in workbench/finder_qt.py. Then python -m unittest -v tests_integrated.test_whole_words gives 'Ran 5 tests ... OK' in both looks. tools/check_finder_ui.py run through check_hatch.ui_checks with GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE=kasandra fails at line 221: "QHeaderView:section 'Date Modified' needs 115 px, has 106".

summary: The patch applies clean. I reproduced the builder's results exactly: 30 modules with 562 tests per look, with only the known test_faces_find_light failing in the Kasandra look, and 22 of 22 window checks passing in both looks with 287 steps each. Three of the new guards fail when the piece they guard is reverted: the Card line fold, the removed toggle, and the window-check lists. Two things must change before merge. First, the pane-width step folded from the retired frame check was cut to 20 pt to dodge a real fault, and nothing in the code or docs says so. A single 14 -> 28 -> 14 pt trip leaves both panes 415 px instead of 326 (479 instead of 354 in the Kasandra look), on the base tree too, which contradicts the report's claim that a direct trip comes back. Second, the Date Modified fix in FinderPage.scale_columns is not pinned by any unit test: reverting it leaves test_whole_words green in both looks, and only check_finder_ui in the Kasandra look catches it. The should_fix list is smaller things: F11 round-trip coverage lost silently, retired names left in two docs pages, inconsistent stale-check counts, raw zero-width characters in a test, a slower gate that runs one look, temp folders the checks leave behind, a merge conflict with look.patch on check_head_ui.py, and printed shortcuts outside the patch.
